bounds: Lifecycle has two request identities, two listener identities, two allocated callbacks, and queue capacity two. A separate overflow instance admits seventeen requests to the real capacity-sixteen FIFO with no listeners. Each listener mounts once. Callback invocation/return are split to expose reentrant delivery. Identities and dispatch epochs never wrap.

assumptions: No exactly-once effect contract is assumed for arbitrary callbacks. A listener can apply a partial effect and retire before its returned promise settles. The real helper suite reproduces effect repetition.

Each per-request effect count is monotone. An eventual suffix with at most one effect is therefore impossible once the duplicated-effect witness occurs. This formulation retains an explicit loop for the negative temporal checker.
No settlement fairness is assumed for an external promise owned by an unmounted listener. Its applying flag can block a replacement forever.
